assumptions: Browser localStorage or equivalent client-side persistence is acceptable (no server-side storage required)
Modern browser support for ES6+ features and accessibility APIs
Single-page HTML/CSS/JS implementation is sufficient (no build process complexity needed for XS scope)
WCAG 2.1 AA compliance is the target accessibility standard
Keyboard navigation includes Enter/Space for button activation and Tab for focus movement
candidate_scope: The minimum viable scope is a single-page web application containing: A numerical counter display, Increment and decrement buttons with proper ARIA labels and keyboard support, Local persistence to maintain count across page refreshes, Semantic HTML structure supporting screen readers, Visual feedback for keyboard focus states, Basic documentation for local startup and accessibility testing.
evidence_refs: Cell input constraints: deploymentExcluded=true, humanAcceptanceAfterLocalStart=true, localRunRequired=true
Trusted provider bindings for deterministic evidence: local runnability v1, accessible counter sandbox check v1, authorized verification observer v1
observed_context: The bounded context consists of a factory-start initiated discovery case for a web application (XS complexity) with the following characteristics: Project is Factory sandbox production-run-001, Epic REQ-001, Constraints are deployment excluded, local run required, human acceptance after local start required, Trusted Evidence Providers include deterministic evidence providers for local runnability, accessibility compliance, and authorized verification, Current State has no existing artifacts, notes, or repository checkouts - this is a greenfield initiative.
problem_statement: This project addresses the need for a simple, accessible counter web application that demonstrates fundamental web development capabilities while prioritizing inclusive design. The problem represents a foundational use case for building accessible web interfaces that can be operated through multiple interaction methods (mouse, keyboard, and assistive technologies).
rationale: The recommendation to proceed is based on: 1) Clear scope boundaries with XS complexity matching the requirements, 2) Strong alignment between the use case (simple counter) and learning objectives (accessibility patterns), 3) Sufficient constraint definition (local run, keyboard support, persistence) without ambiguity, 4) Available trusted evidence providers for validation and acceptance, 5) No critical blockers or missing requirements that would necessitate a clarification phase. The project represents a well-bounded opportunity to demonstrate accessible web development fundamentals with clear success criteria and available validation mechanisms.
risks: Technical: Browser localStorage quota limitations or privacy settings may prevent persistence
Accessibility: Incomplete ARIA implementation or keyboard trap scenarios could exclude users
Adoption: Without proper documentation, the accessibility patterns may not be discoverable or reusable
Verification: Manual human acceptance process may create subjective validation criteria
Local Run: Environmental differences across local development setups could affect reproducibility
stakeholders_or_actors: End users who need a simple counter application accessible via keyboard and assistive technologies
Accessibility stakeholders requiring WCAG-compliant interface patterns
Local deployment and validation stakeholders who will verify the application runs without external dependencies
Development team members who will use this as a reference for accessibility patterns
unknowns: Specific browser compatibility requirements and supported versions
Whether internationalization (i18n) requirements exist for the counter display
Exact accessibility testing methodology and assistive technology combinations to be validated
Performance expectations for local persistence across different browsers
Whether offline functionality beyond local persistence is required
